newsitem.title: singapore: Asian crude steady but outlook weak, buyers absent.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude steady but outlook weak, buyers absent.

text.p: Asian crude prices were mostly steady on Monday but the outlook was weak as bidders held back from the market.
A flurry of West African deals last week, which has depressed sales of Middle East crude and regional crudes, showed few signs of abating Monday.
Traders said ADNOC and Qatar grades were offered at a small premium to official selling prices but bidders were absent.
Oman was offered at MPM -10 cents, but buyers said they expected offer prices to fall further because of the relatively uncompetitive Oman/Dubai differential of $1.00.
Two China players exchanged Oman last week at MPM -5 cents.

Tapis was traded one to two weeks ago at OSP +2 cents for a Japanese trader into Myanmar, a producer confirmed. Traders said the deal further illustrated the market's difficulty valuing Tapis against Tapis swaps values.
Based on a May Cossack, which was sold two weeks ago at APPI Tapis less 40 cents, May loading Tapis was valued around 40 cents, market players said.
China was showing more buying presence for the current month trading, having purchased 300,000 barrels of Widuri at ICP +5/+10 cents and 300,000 barrels of Cinta at ICP flat/+5 cents.
China was also said to have bought Minas as high as ICP +20 cents, despite the fact there were counter offers as low as +10 cents.
Traders said they expected Minas to achieve a modest premium for May trading but doubted the crude would go much higher.
"There is still crude to be sold. If there is buying interest above the ICP, the crude will come out. If below the ICP, I feel sellers have the flexibility to hold back," one seller said.
